findings.body: The link is rendered with the 70% lightened primary color instead of its previous 30% lightened primary color, making it substantially more faded than the intended metadata styling.
findings.failure_mode: The desktop topic metadata link loses its intended visual contrast in light themes and gets the inverse dark-theme shade.
findings.impact: The link is rendered with the 70% lightened primary color instead of its previous 30% lightened primary color, making it substantially more faded than the intended metadata styling.
findings.root_cause: The conversion reverses the intended lightness values for this existing 30% primary-color rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` to preserve the existing light-theme value and provide its dark-theme counterpart.
findings.title: Restore the topic metadata link's original light-theme contrast
findings.trigger: A desktop topic page renders the author/topic metadata link under a light theme.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows L291 changed from 30% to 70% lightness for light theme. The new code `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` inverts the original 30% value, making the link more faded in light themes.

findings.body: The indicator uses the inverse of its former 70% primary shade in light themes and the inverse dark-theme secondary shade, producing inconsistent styling with the desktop flag modal.
findings.failure_mode: The mobile flag message counter is styled with an unintended contrast level and diverges from the desktop equivalent.
findings.impact: The indicator uses the inverse of its former 70% primary shade in light themes and the inverse dark-theme secondary shade, producing inconsistent styling with the desktop flag modal.
findings.root_cause: The conversion swapped the 70%/30% lightness pair to 30%/70%.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, as used by the desktop counterpart.
findings.title: Keep the mobile flag message counter's intended muted shade
findings.trigger: A user opens a flag modal on mobile and the custom-message length indicator is displayed.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows L102 changed from 70% to 30% lightness for light theme.
